speaker: Doctor
text: When did your fever and abdominal pain begin, and are you currently experiencing any vaginal discharge with an unusual odor? Have you had any recent surgeries or deliveries that might be contributing to these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or burning sensation when you urinate, and are you currently having any difficulty emptying your bladder completely? I will also check for costovertebral angle tenderness to rule out a kidney infection. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the uterine tenderness and prolonged labor, I suspect endometritis, so I am ordering a Complete Blood Count to check for leukocytosis. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you currently experiencing any chills, rigors, or noticing a foul-smelling lochia? I will also examine your abdomen to assess the extent of the tenderness and check for any signs of peritoneal irritation.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will proceed with a pelvic exam to assess for cervical motion tenderness and check for any retained placental fragments. Given the prolonged labor and uterine tenderness, I am also requesting a pelvic ultrasound to evaluate the uterine cavity. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the pelvic ultrasound is normal, ruling out retained products, I suspect the urinary symptoms point to a concurrent urinary tract infection. REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: With the ultrasound and urine culture normal, I am shifting focus to the bowel given the decreased sounds and abdominal tenderness. I suspect pelvic abscess or ileus, so I will request a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to visualize any hidden collections. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT scan rules out an abscess or ileus, and the negative urine tests exclude a UTI, leaving endometritis as the primary diagnosis given the fever, uterine tenderness, and prolonged labor history. I will proceed with treatment for endometritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometritis
